Subject: SpectraEdge POC: implementation commitments & next steps

Hi Lena / Rahul —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have aligned owners and a tight timeline for the POC. Please read through and confirm or flag anything missing.

High-level objective
- Validate inference runtime and extraction quality for SpectraEdge search enrichment use case (entity extraction + rerank).

Success criteria (proposed)
- Functional: intent/entity extraction F1 >= 0.87 on the shared validation set (10k annotated rows).
- Latency: median end-to-end (512-token prompt) < 200ms for hosted endpoints, <120ms on Dedicated config.
- Throughput: sustained 50 qps with <1% error rate for batched traffic.
- Integration: streaming responses for multi-part tool-calling and structured JSON output (schema v1) validated against 100 test flows.

POC evaluation plan
- Week 0 (Aug 18–20): sandbox integration — SDK + test harness ingestion of a 1k sample.
- Week 1 (Aug 21–27): full integration of API routes, instrument KV cache, and run 5k validation cases.
- Week 2 (Aug 28–Sep 3): quality regression runs, latency tuning, and final acceptance run.

Ownership
- Redwood: Ben Carter (sales/KR) — overall POC lead, contact for timelines and procurement; Marissa Cole (eng) — SDK & test harness; Sergio Alvarez (solutions) — deployment templates and performance tuning.
- SpectraEdge: Lena Wu — PM; Rahul Singh — infra/ops lead.

Integration notes (tech highlights)
- SDK options: JS (browser/node) and Python (server). We will supply a small JS snippet for streaming and a Python example for batched inference.
- API routes: POST /v1/generate (sync), /v1/stream (SSE/WebSocket) — we recommend WebSocket for multi-tool sequences.
- Streaming: supports SSE and WebSocket; hosted API has token-based short sessions (recommended for sandbox). For Dedicated/Private we can enable persistent WS with higher throughput.
- Tool calling: we will send an example mapping for your internal tools (client->tool registry->function calls) and a JSON schema for structured outputs.

Attachments attached: spectraedge_poc_success_criteria.xlsx, integration_api_contract_v1.pdf

Ask / next steps (please reply in-thread)
1) Confirm success criteria and POC acceptance window.
2) Confirm sandbox kickoff date — propose Aug 18 morning (PST).
3) Please share a small sample (1k rows) and an SFTP/Drive link for ingestion tests.

I’ll create a HubSpot milestone and a short project board once we confirm.

Thanks — talk soon.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

We’ve got a 1k sample ready; I’ll share the Drive link once we confirm the kickoff. Aug 18 morning PST works for us.

Hi Lena — quick answers inline.

Streaming
- WebSocket is our recommended path for multi-step tool-calls. On your side you just need an outbound WS client that can reconnect; we’ll provide a small client example (JS) and a connector for your annotator. We also support SSE if you prefer simpler one-way streaming.

Dedicated / VPC
- Sandbox tokens: we can provision a Dedicated sandbox for the POC. The token provisioning and endpoints will be different; they are scoped to the Dedicated subdomain but the SDK usage is identical. Sergio will prepare a Dedicated test endpoint and provide DNS + token instructions.

Sandbox tokens & test accounts
- We will issue ephemeral tokens scoped to the POC and limited to the sample dataset. Expect a short doc: sandbox_token_instructions.txt attached.

Next step: I’ll loop Sergio to kick off endpoint provisioning and Marissa will start the SDK snippet. Proposed internal owners below. If Aug 18 AM PST works we’ll schedule a 30m technical kickoff focused on connectivity and test-token issuance.

Ben

Attachments: sandbox_token_instructions.txt

Adding technical deliverables and dates from the engineering side so SpectraEdge knows what to expect: 

Marissa's POC deliverables (Redwood)- Aug 17 EOD: JS streaming snippet + Python batch example (public gist + npm package pointer).- Aug 19 EOD: test-harness Docker image (ingest sample, run 1k flows, generate perf report).- Aug 25: recommended runtime config (KV cache settings, batching thresholds, quantization profile) and a short perf-run report.

Implementation checklist (brief)
- SDK: import + init example, call pattern for /v1/generate and /v1/stream, reconnect strategy for WS.
- API: schema v1 for structured outputs attached in integration_api_contract_v1.pdf.
- Tool-calling: we will provide a mapping table (client event -> Redwood function signature) and a sample tool adapter for your annotator.
- Observability: we’ll push a tracing hook and a small trace collection script so you can see per-request token costs in your sandbox.

Notes & recommendations
- For best throughput on your 50 qps target use batching window of 20–40ms with a max batch size of 16 for 512-token prompts.
- Use our recommended quantization profile for Dedicated if you need to reduce GPU memory while preserving accuracy — I’ll attach a short note with numbers on Aug 25.

I’ll publish the snippets to a private repo and share links in the kickoff. If your infra team needs a pre-built Docker image of the client we can supply one.
